info.name: Dhun API
info.description:
Maintained alongside the code. Any endpoint change — added, removed, renamed, new field, new error code — updates this collection in the SAME change. A stale collection is a broken build.

## Conventions

- Every route lives under `/{{apiVersion}}/` (currently v1). Old app versions stay alive forever, so the prefix is never retrofitted.
- Auth is `Bearer {{accessToken}}`, set once at collection level and inherited.
- **Every money endpoint requires an `Idempotency-Key` header** (a UUID). The collection pre-request script generates one automatically for any request whose URL contains `/wallet/`, `/gifts/`, `/cosmetics/` or `/payouts/`.
- `X-Trace-Id` is echoed back on every response and included in every error body. Quote it in bug reports.

## Error envelope

Every failure looks like this:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE", "message": "...", "details": {}, "trace_id": "..." } }
```

Switch on `code`, never on the HTTP status or the message.

## Folder status

Folders map to milestones in `docs/build-plan.md`. Empty ones are not yet built — they are here so the structure is agreed before the endpoints land.

## Errors

Every failure uses the same envelope. Switch on `code`, never on the status or the message.

```json
{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {}, "trace_id": "..." } }
```

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | `details.issues[]` carries `field`, `code`, `message`. Field paths only — your input is never echoed back. |
| `UNSAFE_PAYLOAD` | 400 | Body contained `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` |
| `BAD_JSON` | 400 | Body was not valid JSON |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | Content-Type must be application/json |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Body over 256 KB |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `INVALID_TOKEN` | 401 | Missing or bad bearer token |
| `REGISTRATION_REQUIRED` | 403 | Guest tried to spend — verify a phone first |
| `DOB_REQUIRED` | 403 | **Adult gate.** No date of birth on file. Open the date picker. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Under 18, or missing a role |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Check `Retry-After` and the `RateLimit-*` headers |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` / `_INVALID` | 400 | Money endpoints need a UUID key |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` | 422 | Same key, different operation — a client bug |
| `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` | 402 | |
| `SIGNATURE_INVALID` / `RECEIPT_INVALID` | 402 | Payment did not verify |
| `RECEIPT_ALREADY_USED` | 409 | Receipt redeemed by another account |
| `TXN_TYPE_INACTIVE` | 503 | Kill switch is on for that flow |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / `TIMEOUT` | 503 / 504 | Transient — safe to retry |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Always generic. Quote the `trace_id`. |

## Security

- **Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored.** A typo'd key returns 422 rather than being silently dropped.
- **Rate limits** apply per IP, per device and per user. Guest creation is 5/hour per device; money endpoints 30/min per user.
- **Money endpoints require a registered adult.** Authenticated, phone-verified, and 18+ with a date of birth on file.
- 5xx messages are always generic. The detail is in the logs against your `trace_id`.

exec: // Money endpoints must carry an Idempotency-Key. Generating it here means
// it is never forgotten by hand, and re-sending the same request in Postman
// exercises a genuine new operation rather than an accidental replay.
// One trace id per request, echoed back by the server.
// Applies to every request in the collection.

item.name: Health
item.description: Unversioned on purpose — infrastructure probes should not care about API versions.

request.description: Is the process up? Used by the load balancer. Never touches the database.
Can it actually serve? Checks Postgres. Returns 503 when the pool is dead, so a broken instance is pulled from rotation rather than failing user requests.
Proves the error envelope is wired up before any real endpoint exists.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Phone OTP with WhatsApp primary and SMS fallback, JWT access + rotating refresh, guest upgraded in place.

**Run them in order.** Each request saves what the next one needs into the environment, so the whole signup flow works end to end without copying tokens by hand.

`devCode` is returned by the OTP request outside production, which is what makes this runnable before TRAI DLT registration completes.

request.description: Anonymous but real identity, called on first launch. The user can watch, follow and earn free coins before signing up — and keeps all of it, because signup fills in this same row rather than replacing it.
Rate limited to 5 per number per hour. Requesting a new code immediately invalidates the previous one.

exec: // Only present outside production — the console provider logs it there.

request.description:
Sends the guest access token, so the guest is upgraded IN PLACE and keeps its user id. Without a token a brand new registered user is created instead.

If the number already belongs to an account, that account is signed into and the guest row is left alone — balances are never merged between two identities.
Current user with their active scoped role grants.

Sets the profile. **A date of birth is required before any money endpoint will work** — hard rule #5 is enforced where money moves, not just as an optional field, so it cannot be bypassed by skipping the question.

Every session response now carries `user.profileComplete` — display name AND date of birth both set. The client cannot work this out alone because it never sees the date of birth, and without it someone who quit mid-signup came back authenticated and was never asked again.

An under-18 date returns 403 UNDERAGE. Without one, purchases return 403 DOB_REQUIRED so the app knows to open the date picker.

Age is evaluated against the calendar date in IST, so someone turning 18 today passes from 00:00 IST. A date that matches the YYYY-MM-DD shape but is not a real date (`2000-02-31`), or one in the future, returns 422 INVALID_DOB — not UNDERAGE, because a typo must not send a user into an age-appeal flow.

Rotates: the presented token is retired and a new pair issued.

Presenting an already-rotated token means two parties hold it, so the entire device chain is revoked and the response is 401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED. Try running this twice in a row to see it.
Revokes refresh tokens for this device, or every device with allDevices: true. The access token stays valid until it expires — that is the trade for stateless auth.

item.name: Catalog
item.description:
Server-driven config. Day-1 non-negotiable #6: adding a gift or changing a price must never need an app release, because old app versions stay alive forever.

Cached 30s in process; an admin edit clears it immediately.

request.description:
20 gifts across 5 tiers, repriced for 55 coins/rupee.

`payoutRateBp` is PER GIFT, never a global constant, so event gifts can carry a different rate later.

Priced in GEMS. Zero host payout — this is the margin path.

VIP tiers are seeded but inactive (Phase 1), so they do not appear here.

item.name: Wallet
item.description:
Balances, packs, purchases and the coins-to-gems conversion.

**Every endpoint here that moves money requires `Idempotency-Key`** — the collection pre-request script generates one automatically.

For purchases the header is NOT what makes it safe: the ledger key is derived from the receipt, so replaying a captured receipt under a fresh key still credits exactly once. Send request 3 twice with the same `purchaseToken` to see `replayed: true`.

request.description:
Coins, gems, user level, and lifetime purchased coins.

Level accrues on PURCHASE, not on spend — free coins are ordinary coins now, so scoring on spend would let daily check-ins be ground into levels.

The 55 coins/rupee table. Totals match the source doc so advertised value is preserved; only the coin/gem split is new.

Starter is deliberately off-formula (105 coins/rupee) — its job is teaching the gifting loop, not margin.

With `IAP_PROVIDER=stub` a token shaped `stub-xxxxxxxx` is accepted without calling Google, so the whole path works before the Play developer account exists.

The real Google Play verifier is blocked on the M3 spike.

Signature is verified offline: Razorpay signs `order_id|payment_id` with the account key secret, so this path needs no spike and no network call.

The web channel has its own cash account, which is how channel mix becomes a balance read rather than a report.

ONE WAY, +20%. This is the lever that pulls blended payout down: coins pay hosts 30% of face value, gems pay nothing.

There is deliberately no reverse. Gems converting back to coins would let a whale turn cosmetics money into giftable coins and the payout design collapses.
Read from the ledger, joined only on the caller own scoped accounts — a user can never see a system account or another person movements.
Includes status, so a purchase stuck at `pending` (a crash between the receipt and the credit) is visible rather than silent.

item.name: Rooms — M5
item.description:
Room lifecycle and seats. Live chat and presence run over the WebSocket gateway, not REST.

Planned: `GET /v1/rooms`, `POST /v1/rooms`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/join`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/seats/{index}`, `DELETE /v1/rooms/{id}/seats/{index}`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/go-live`, `POST /v1/rooms/{id}/end`.

item.name: Gifting — M6
item.description:
Money endpoints — `Idempotency-Key` required.

Planned: `GET /v1/gifts/catalog` (server-driven; adding a gift must never need an app release), `POST /v1/gifts/send` (identity: gift_id, host_id, room_id, quantity), `GET /v1/gifts/leaderboard/{roomId}`.

item.name: Cosmetics — M7
item.description:
Priced in gems only. Zero host payout — this is the margin path.

Planned: `GET /v1/cosmetics/catalog`, `POST /v1/cosmetics/purchase`, `GET /v1/cosmetics/owned`, `POST /v1/cosmetics/equip`.

item.name: Host & Payouts — M8
item.description:
Verification and withdrawals. Maker-checker is enforced by the system, not by policy — one person can never both prepare and approve.

Planned: `POST /v1/host/apply`, `POST /v1/host/verify/pan`, `POST /v1/host/verify/bank`, `POST /v1/host/verify/face`, `GET /v1/host/earnings`, `POST /v1/payouts/request`, `GET /v1/payouts`.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Ships with every milestone rather than as a phase of its own — the docs are explicit that the admin panel is part of the MVP.

Planned: catalog editing (M4), room monitoring (M5), payout approval (M8), moderator dashboard (M9), and transaction-type kill switches (`PATCH /v1/admin/txn-types/{code}` — flipping `is_active` stops a money flow platform-wide with no deploy).

request.description:
The feed the app opens on. **No session required** — browsing is the top of the funnel and a signed-out user must see what the app is before being asked for a phone number.

`category=explore` returns single-host rooms, `party` returns rooms with seats, `following` needs a session and returns EMPTY without one rather than silently ignoring the filter.

Ended rooms never appear. `trending` marks the top ten by viewers and is computed in the same query, so it can never disagree with the order.

Private by definition — 401 without a session.

Unread is counted from the participant's read WATERMARK, not a stored counter: a counter has to be decremented correctly from several places and drifts the first time one is missed.

`filter` is one of all | official | unread | groups.

Everything the Me screen shows that is not a balance: follower counts, unseen profile visitors, level, and the withdrawable points balance.

`friends` is a follow in BOTH directions, computed rather than stored so it can never disagree with the follow rows.

`verified` means PHONE verified, which is what gates money endpoints today. The payout KYC badge — PAN plus face match, hard rule #5 — is a stricter, separate check that arrives with payouts in M8.

`publicId` is the short number a user reads out to be found. Never the internal uuid.

The campaign strip above the feed. Server-driven from day one (non-negotiable #6): a campaign must never need an app release, and a bad banner is killed in seconds by flipping `is_active`.

Expired banners are filtered by the query, not by a sweep — a banner whose countdown has run out is worse than no banner.

⚠️ HARD RULE #1: `action` is a CLOSED set (ranking | rewards | topup | none). An event may be a ranking; it may never be chance. No lucky box, no wheel, no mystery gift.

IDEMPOTENT — following twice is a no-op, not a 409. A double tap on a slow connection is the common case, and an error there would be shown to a user who did exactly the right thing.

Allowed for a GUEST: a guest is a real server-side identity, and following is the retention loop that gives them a reason to come back. Rate-limited to 200/hour per USER — far above any human, far below a script building a graph.

422 CANNOT_FOLLOW_SELF, 404 USER_NOT_FOUND.
Also idempotent. Unfollowing someone you never followed is not an error.
Who looked at your profile, newest first, each with whether you already follow them — so the button renders correctly without a second call.

Clears the "N new" badge and returns how many were cleared.

POST rather than GET because it CHANGES STATE: a GET that mutates gets fired by a prefetcher and clears a badge nobody looked at.

Upserted, not appended — the question is "who has been looking", not "how many times", and append-only grows without bound for a popular host.

Re-visiting refreshes the timestamp AND clears seen_at, so a returning visitor surfaces again.

Visiting your own profile is silently ignored: the client cannot always know whose profile it is opening. 204 No Content.
Membership is checked in the WHERE clause, not by a separate lookup — one query that returns nothing for a non-member cannot be raced by a membership change between the check and the read.

Moves the read WATERMARK to now. Idempotent, so it is safe on every open, and still correct after a message is deleted — which a counter is not.

404 for a thread you are not in, NOT 403: telling a stranger that a thread exists but is not theirs is itself a leak.

Force-update floor and remote feature flags — day-1 non-negotiable #5.

ANONYMOUS on purpose: a force-update has to reach a user who cannot sign in, which is exactly the situation a broken auth release creates.

Flags here are the NON-money switches. The money layer has a stronger one — ledger_txn_types.is_active stops a flow inside the transaction — so a client that ignores a flag, or a modified build that never asks, still cannot move coins.

Non-boolean flag values are dropped rather than passed through.

What a STRANGER may see — deliberately narrower than your own summary: no points balance, no unseen-visitor count, no date of birth, no phone. Deciding what a stranger sees is a trust-and-safety question, so a field is absent until someone decides it should be there.

Returns 404 when either party has blocked the other, and for a banned account. NOT 403 — a 403 confirms the account exists.

Store review REQUIRES a working report mechanism for user-generated content. This is the intake half; queue triage, strikes and appeals are M9.

`reason` is a CLOSED set mapped to the policy levels in trust-and-safety-v1 — free text alone cannot be triaged, counted, or turned into a threshold that pages someone.

One row per reporter per subject per day. Twenty people reporting the same host is the strongest signal moderation has; one person reporting twenty times is not. A same-day repeat returns `filed: false` and still 202, because telling a user off for reporting teaches them not to.

202 Accepted, not 201: the report is recorded, and whether it results in anything is a human decision later.

Takes effect immediately and in BOTH directions — neither party sees the other's rooms in any feed. A one-way block that leaves the blocked person able to watch is a mute, not a block.

Does NOT unfollow: blocking and unfollowing are separate intentions, and a user who blocks then unblocks should not silently lose a follow they chose.

This is the remedy a user can apply without waiting for a moderator, which matters because the gap between reporting and review is hours at best.
Idempotent.
